candidate_relations.reason: Papillary angioma names the same benign papillary vascular tumor represented by ectatic vessels and branching intravascular papillae.
Histology shows a circumscribed endothelial neoplasm with structured intravascular papillae rather than malformed mature vessels.
The swollen endothelial covering and papillary growth are organized without atypia or infiltrative behavior needed for angioendothelioma.
No hobnail endothelial cells, hemosiderin, or targetoid clinical morphology is described; the defining feature is branching papillae with hyaline globules.
Hemangioma captures the benign blood-vessel lineage but omits the distinctive intravascular papillary architecture.
HHV-8 staining is negative and the lesion is a small circumscribed tumor without spindle-cell slit-like vasculature.
CD31-positive tumor vessels establish a vascular tumor, but this umbrella label loses the papillary hemangioma subtype.
The candidate includes vascular lineage and scalp location but not the papillary structures, PAS-positive globules, and pericytic cores.

Papillary endothelial hyperplasia is typically a thrombus-associated reactive process, whereas the specimen is described as a well-circumscribed vascular tumor with characteristic endothelial globules.
The record emphasizes swollen endothelial cells lining branching papillae rather than solid lobules of epithelioid endothelial cells with inflammatory stroma.
The red scalp nodule lacks a targetoid ring and histology lacks the hobnail, hemosiderotic pattern of targetoid hemosiderotic hemangioma.
Smooth-muscle actin highlights only papillary pericytes while the neoplastic vessels themselves are CD31-positive, excluding glomus tumor.
